title: Condo Sinking Fund and Common Area Fees in Phuket
description: What the common area fee and sinking fund pay for, how they are billed in Phuket condos, with published amounts from projects in our catalogue.
h1: Condo Sinking Fund and Common Area Fees
intro: After you buy a condo you pay ongoing costs to maintain the shared parts of the building. Two items appear most often: a recurring common area fee and a sinking fund. Amounts differ by project, so this guide shows what we have recorded from developer materials and how to compare them.

sections.h2: Juristic person and what it does
p: A registered condominium has a juristic person that manages the common property: lifts, pool, gardens, security, cleaning and insurance. Owners pay for it through fees decided under the building’s rules.

The common area fee, often called CAM, is billed monthly or yearly. Many Phuket condos bill it per square metre of the unit, others use a fixed amount. Ask what it covers (water, cleaning, security, pool) and what is billed separately (electricity, internet, parking).

The sinking fund is a reserve for large future repairs and replacements. It is commonly a one-off payment at transfer, though some buildings collect it over time. Ask how it is held and who can spend it.
The table lists every project where we recorded a published figure. Units differ, so check the original wording.
p2: Example for orientation only: a project that charges THB 70 per square metre per month, for a unit of 50 square metres, would bill THB 3,500 per month. Use the real figure and the real unit size for your case.

ul: Convert every fee to a monthly amount for your unit size.
Ask what services the fee includes and how often it has changed.
Ask whether the building has a sinking fund balance and how it is audited.
Compare the fee with the amenities: a large pool and gym cost more to run.
